text_fidelity_a:
Discover with Dr. Cool PRO Series Rock Tumbler - Turn Rocks into Stunning Gemstones! At first I put this in the kitchen, I quickly learned that it was too loud for an open floor plan, it made me listen to tv on too high of a volume, so when I switched to the 2nd grit I moved it to a spare bedroom. This worked out great since I go in that room almost daily I was able to keep up with knowing when to change out to the next grit.

This is super easy to set up and get started. It comes with absolutely everything needed to go from start to finish including jewelry items to use so you can show off your stones. The instructions are very easy to follow along too.It also comes with activity books and the jewelry pieces are a necklace, a ring, a keychain and ear rings.

The instructions gives you an idea of how long the stones should tumble in each grit and at what speed.
This is what I did..
-grit #1..I did for 3 days on #3 speed
-grit#2.. I started at 5 days on #2…then opened it up and decided it needed a few more days since they were a bit rough so I did 2
more days on #3 setting
-grit#3.. I did for 7 days on #1 setting.
-grit#4..I did 7 days on #1. The smaller stones were great , the larger stones had a few blemishes yet, but I like things when they
aren’t perfect so they were great for me…I will be making them into necklaces once I put holes in them.

As you can see from my pictures from start to finish how much the rocks changed. Then at the end I wiped them off with mineral oil as suggested in the instructions. This has been an amazing experience to watch the rough rocks transform into smooth beautiful stones.
text_fidelity_b: Discover with Dr. Cool PRO Series Rock Tumbler - Turn Rocks into Stunning Gemstones!

ThinkFun and Crazy Aaron's Thinking Putty Puzzle and STEM Toy for Boys and Girls Ages 8 and Up - The Famous Thinking Putty in Logic Game Form I’ve played many of Thinkfun’s logic puzzles, and use them in my classroom. So, I was very interested in their new logic puzzle that uses Crazy Aaron’s Putty. This game has some similarities with their other logic puzzles. It comes with 60 cards that show the challenge setup on one side and a possible answer on the back. The setup for each challenge takes the longest than any other logic puzzle because you have to tear the balls of putty off each color. It is challenging, even the first few challenges’ solutions aren’t immediately visible, they take some thought to solve.

I enjoyed this for myself and found it relaxing to put together and solve. I could see some kids not having the patience to play through the puzzle. I don’t plan to use this one in my classroom because I think the putty would get funky after having some kids play with it, and there could be some putty mixing that intentionally or unintentionally could happen and ruin the game.

Overall, this is a very clever idea. I’ve played the beginning challenges and enjoyed figuring them out. Kids will love the putty, but I’m not sure how long the challenges will hold their attention.
text_fidelity_b: ThinkFun and Crazy Aaron's Thinking Putty Puzzle and STEM Toy for Boys and Girls Ages 8 and Up - The Famous Thinking Putty in Logic Game Form

text_fidelity_a: Backyard Discovery Sweetwater All Cedar White Modern Outdoor Wooden Playhouse, Cottage, Sink, Stove, Windows, Kitchen with Pot and Pans and Utensils, Flowerpot Holders, Working Doorbell, Ages 2-6 We've had this playhouse for a couple of months and it still looks brand new - despite the Iowa sun, our extreme heat and rain and freezes.  When we opened up the package, we had a couple of issues with the wood being cracked.  The overall setup is fairly easy if you follow the directions.  Customer service was really great working with when I called to get replacement parts.  To be clear, though, I wasn't aware that we'd have to seal the playhouse.  I only found that out because I'd called for replacement parts.  We used a marine sealant and it is full waterproofing!  We used a chemical pump sprayer to apply it (we sprayed it on and then brushed over it - it is very runny like milk and goes on white but dries clear).  I, originally, expected the wood to be pre-sealed since it was a playhouse specifically for outside.  So, in hindsight, I am very grateful that we talked with the helpful customer service person.  Otherwise, we'd probably have to be replacing the house next year ... and, I wouldn't have been very happy with the purchase.  However, we've had it a couple months now and it still looks brand new!  I'd highly recommend this playhouse IF you are willing to seal it.  Yes, marine clear coat is expensive but so was the playhouse.  All in all, a great addition to our backyard and I'm sure we'll get several years of grandchildren's fun with it!

Monopoly Here and Now World Edition Game This game is played a bit different than the regular Monopoly games. There are some similarities though. You get four tokens (and passports), so that seems to limit the number of people who can play. The object of the game is to collect passport stamps - the person to fill their passport first wins. The game starts off with all the major stamps placed on the board - a specific sized one for each property. There are some generic gray stamps that stay in the bank. Landing on a spot you have the option to buy that stamp or it can get auctioned off. When a player lands on a spot that you have the stamp for - the owner is paid a 'Visitor Fee' (basically like rent in the regular game). Another difference are the Here & Now cards and the Chance cards. I think these are what makes the game fun to play. The things the cards can let you do makes the game challenging - just when you think you're going to get ahead, another player can use one of their cards and put a damper on your play. Makes for some lively social interactions (if you get my drift). The dice is a bit different - one die has a icon in the place of the 1 pip (sort of reminds me of the speed die). That icon is the 'Sneaky Swap', it can also still be the 1 in some rolls.

Overall I have to say I've enjoyed trying out this new game (can't say the same for everybody here). I think we're still getting use to the way the game plays compared to regular Monopoly. The games tend to be a bit short - about an hour, but that might be because we still stop a bit and look at the rules to figure out what we're doing. Plus, given the different international locations on the board, we sometimes stop and an go look up where something is. (Helps to keep a globe handy). Fun game - and a bit educational.
text_fidelity_b: Monopoly Here and Now World Edition Game

The Chameleon, Award-Winning Board Game for Families & Friends…… If you're familiar with the game Spyfall, then you're going to be able to jump right into this game. This one is quirkier, faster, but fortunately, has more replayability than Spyfall does.

In The Chameleon, each player is given a code card, or a card that says "You're the Chameleon." If you have a code card, you look up a word on a shared board, and if you're The Chameleon, you attempt to blend in with everyone else. After a little bit of finding and thinking time, each player says one word, even the Chameleon. Each player is then to attempt to argue and deduce who the Chameleon player is. Everyone votes, and that player is revealed. If it's not the Chameleon, then that player has done a good job of blending in and is the winner of the round. If it is the Chameleon, then that player gets the opportunity to guess the secret word that everyone else knew. If they get it right, they win. If not, everyone else wins.

Rounds of this game are fast, and that's a great thing. After repeat plays, it becomes fairly easy to identify the Chameleon player, but that's when the game really starts. Were you vague enough with your words so that they cannot figure out the secret code word?

There is enough replayability in this box to make the game fun for a wide range of groups, and a larger number of players. There are 40 different category clues, which means that there are 640 different possible words you could have, and that far exceeds the 20 locations of Spyfall.

Two issues prevent this from being a 5* game. The first is component quality. It's bad. Cards are awkwardly sized and flimsy, there are remainder marks on the edges of some cards from where they were cut. The second issue is that there simply aren't enough mapping location cards in the box. There's really only two possible sets of locations, and while there are no players who will be able to memorize the exact locations of words, it's possible that repeat mappings occur, and Chameleons with outstanding memories will be able to guess with regularity by reading the dice.
text_fidelity_b: The Chameleon, Award-Winning Board Game for Families & Friends……

text_fidelity_a:
Harry Potter Lexicon-GO! Word Game Lexicon Go is a very fast-paced, easy-to-play word game using a deck of 52 plastic tiles, each with a letter of the alphabet. the tiles are arranged face down on the playing area, and each player draws 10 tiles from the deck. The goal is to arrange all 10 of your tiles into words as quickly as possible. If you're unable to use all of your letters to make words, you can swap out a tile (within certain parameters) or you can play on other players' words. The first player to use all 10 tiles wins the round. Win five rounds and you've won the game.

We played this game with two, three, four, and five adult players. I would guess that in at least 8 out of 10 rounds, one player was able to use all of her letters to form words without any swapping out or playing on another player's tiles -- which made the game move very, very quickly, , but also made it a little bit boring. There is very little strategizing and interaction. The best part was challenging words and learning the meaning of funny new words.

This was a little bit too fast-paced and frenetic for my tastes, and whether you could use all your tiles on the first draw depended primarily on getting a good vowel to consonant ratio- if you draw at least three vowels, it's pretty easy to make two, three, or four letter words to use all ten tiles. If you draw only one or two vowels, you will have a tough time using all your tiles.

The game is fun, clever, and well-made. The carrying case is well-made and the tiles are nice quality. This would be a great family game or vacation game, and it worked equally well with two players as it did with five players -- it just worked differently. It is versatile. If you're a fan of Scrabble or the New York Times crossword, this seems very fast-paced and a little too easy. It may better suited for younger players -- maybe elementary school-aged children.
text_fidelity_b: Harry Potter Lexicon-GO! Word Game

HUBSAN X4 H107C HD 2MP Camera 2.4G 4CH 6 Axis Gyro RC Quadcopter Red/White (PH-H107C) At first I received the SD version instead of the HD version from one seller on Amazon. I returned it.The Little One's Choice got it right and sent me the HD version for which I had paid. Make sure you get what you paid for. It should say "HD Camera" in big letters on the Hubsan box. Unfortunately, the correct one they sent had horrible very dark lines in the video in all types of lighting conditions. I had to return it. The replacement was fine.

My "review" is going to be a bit rambling from an experienced guy to those who are tying to get started in this hobby. My hope is that I might have something to say that the old-timers might find useful as well.

My short review in this paragraph is that this quad is awesome (overused word, I know, but it fits here) for the price and simply amazing. I've had hours of fun with mine and I own 2 other non-camera Hubsans, one Proto-X and a Blade Quad Nano. This Hubsan quad is the most bang for the buck. I've also got big copters that are gathering dust while I have fun with these small ones. Strangely, I'm not missing them. Did I mention these little things are fun?

It is refreshing to the point of joyfulness to be able to fly this quad around since it is so relatively inexpensive and nimble. I bought several bags of props out of an abundance of caution and have not used one yet. Still, I don't crash much, so if you are new at this, you might need more propellers than the one set provided. I bought some spare batteries (they are blue, sold in a set of 5) and a couple of the Traxxas 2-port chargers. These work fine and let you have more charged batteries handy.

I want to say this quad is easy to fly. For me it is very easy, but it is also fun. I understand that for those who have never flown any type of RC rotor craft that you will have to be serious about learning to use and fly this little thing properly.

Don't be frustrated if you crash a lot at first. Fly in an open area outdoors if possible. If you fly indoors, which I know is a very attractive prospect at first, you will crash into walls and ceiling often and perhaps lose some propellers. At first you may even forget which hand "does what" and crash pretty hard. The body of this quad is tough, but I have seen some photos of broken ones. All of those slammed hard onto concrete walls or slabs.

If a crash is imminent, learn to cut the power immediately. Throttle off completely. You do not want the motors stalling against an obstruction. They will burn out if you abuse them that way. Also, never try to bump the throttle to kick the motors on in an attempt to flip the copter upright if it sets down at an angle. Motivate your body to the quad, pick it up and set it down straight. It will last longer that way.

The rotor guard is taped to the bottom of the tray. Use it if you are unsure of your skills. By the way, when removing the props to put this on, do be sure to hold down the motor body. If it comes up too far the motor wires will snap off. It is only held in place with friction. Use a pinching grasp to pull the prop off. There's a little wrench to help with pulling the props. Use that if one came with your quad. Some people don't get one, I don't know why.

This same type of grasp is also the correct way to disconnect the battery. If you pull by the wires, you will soon have a broken connection. Try to grasp both sides of the connector with your thumbs while you squeeze to persuade the connector away from its mate. Try to make contact with as much connector, not wire, as possible.

There are many videos on YouTube which are instructive for newbies. Especially helpful even for an experienced guy like me was one video that showed how to restore a stuck motor to working condition with a pair of pliers. Especially learn how to reset the gyros with the transmitter and how to zero-out the transmitter itself. Read the instructions carefully and you'll see that you can adjust the sensitivity of the transmitter relative to control input. Learn and understand how to use the trim buttons. There is a lot of info in that little manual. It's not the greatest manual I've seen, but it is a good effort at one and most of the hazy parts are cleared up on YouTube.

I've found that when the lights flash during flight to signal a low battery (time to land!) that the voltage is about 3.7 volts. This is a pretty safe voltage for storing a LiPo so if you are not going to fly again soon don't bother to charge it. Letting a fully charged LiPo sit for more than a week can be hard on it. Take good care of the battery by never flying it to the point where it is dead. In fact, as soon as you get the flashing warning - land! If you are flying outside where you can't see the warning well in daylight, I'd recommend setting a kitchen timer set to 5-1/2 minutes and timing your flights. Better safe than sorry. Once you run a LiPo down too far it's gone or soon will be.

If you have spare batteries all charged up during a flying session, avoid the temptation of replacing an exhausted battery with a fresh one and getting right back up into the air. My opinion is you should let the motors cool down for a few minutes first. They will be very hot after you complete a full flight so give them a chance to cool a bit before you take to the skies again.

They sell higher capacity batteries here on Amazon. I believe they are 500 mAh. I would not recommend them. Any longer flight time potential will be offset by the extra battery weight. Also the motors will have to work harder at higher RPM to keep the quad airborne. I think the stock capacity battery size is well-suited to this quad.

The instructions encourage you to stuff the battery leads up into the copter body so they don't hang out. I just let them hang out. Stuffing them up in there just stresses all the connections and solder joints and the wires don't stay up in there very will anyway. Just my opinion on that one, folks.

The motors are amazing on these little quads. They are good for about 70 hours of actual flying time. That's really pretty good. Still, if you are going to use the quad a lot and put about 100 flights on it, you will eventually have a motor go bad. It is a good idea to have a spaare motor kit. The motors on the 107C are 8.5mm wide. The motors from the 107L will NOT fit. So get the correct ones.

If you have to replace a motor, you'll have to be able to solder or know somebody who can do it for you. It's a simple soldering task for an experienced RC hobbyist so members of that ilk will have no problem. If you are just leaping into RC with this quad and don't have those skills because you haven't had to suffer the school of hard knocks like we old-timers did, you just have to learn soldering or lean on somebody who can do it for you. Some solder and a basic pencil soldering iron can be obtained for less that 20 bucks if you want to learn a new, useful skill.

As for the HD camera, it is quite sufficient. This little camera will never be super stable outdoors in wind but the video is still quite good. In windy conditions, you MUST press down the right stick to get into expert mode. If you don't you will not have sufficient control movement to fight the wind. You will watch helplessly as your copter drifts away from you if you can't bring it down immediately. Incidentally, while in expert mode if you are afraid of flipping the copter because of the unlimited control movement it provides, just click the left stick down to enter "no-flip" mode.

Also regarding the camera, you must follow the correct procedure to obtain video. Turn on your transmitter with the throttle completely off. Insert the SD card. Connect the battery. Wait for the red light to turn off in the SD card slot. All you should see is a tiny blue light (NO red light). Now you can press the little switch on the side to start recording. You'll see the tiny red light flashing. When you finish your video flight, you must press the little switch again to stop the video. Wait for the red light to go out (indicating the video file has been saved. Now you may unplug the battery. If desired you may also unplug the SD card now.

If you don't use the switch to stop the video, or if you unplug the battery while the red light is flashing, you will save no video.

Always plug/unplug the SD card with the battery disconnected! Also, the SD card socket is not like those on many mobile phones with which you may be familiar. There is no "spring action". You just slide the card in until it bottoms in the slot. If you keep pushing it when you feel resistance thinking you are going to push against the locking spring, don't do it. Push too hard and you could harm the card socket. So go easy on it!

It is amazing that we can now buy a gyro-stabilized copter and get it hovering with so little "learning". It was not unusual for people to spend weeks just learning the touch to get a single rotor copter off the ground in one piece and into a hover. Now it is so much cheaper and simpler. I won't say easy, because as I have said if you are absolute noob you have to learn the controls and develop your skills. Still, you should be able to get it off the ground and hover without too much agony.

If you are interested in flying RC, I don't think you can go wrong with giving this quad a try. I feel it is a bargain price and rewarding and fun to learn to fly.
text_fidelity_b: HUBSAN X4 H107C HD 2MP Camera 2.4G 4CH 6 Axis Gyro RC Quadcopter Red/White (PH-H107C)

They are the same material, with the same qualities of thin, close-fitting protection, that are not too slick to stack well, and not too matt to shuffle beautifully. And to top it off, the Panda sleeves are 1mm narrower than the Delphia sleeves and so the fit, for games like Arkham Horror LCG, is even better! (see photo) Absolutely my favorite sleeves, by far! The bonus card boxes, with their handy roll of double-sided modeler's tape, is a friendly gesture. Five Stars.

Takenoko Board Game | Bamboo Farming Game | Panda Themed Strategy Fun Family Game for Adults and Kids | Ages 8+ | 2-4 Players | Average Playtime 45 Minutes | Made by Matagot We had the pleasure of playing this in our most recent game night, and it was delightful. You start with a few "quests" based on bamboo for pandas to eat, bamboo in the "fields", and the arrangement of those "field" tiles (as well as access to water ...). It's actually rather simple. Each turn you get to expand the game by adding field tiles (up adding water or other upgrades to the tiles), grow bamboo, have the panda eat the bamboo, or take on more "quests". As everything but the bamboo the panda eats belongs to everyone, there's a passive cooperation, and other than the score at the end (based on completing those cards), it doesn't feel that competitive. If another player lays down irrigation, that's not irrigation that solely benefits them or takes away from what you have, rather it adds to what you have and may well help complete one of your quests. We played with folks from 7 years old on up, and everyone had a great time.

The only real negative (and I don't see the need to deduct any stars from the rating) is that this is at max a four player game. I could'd imagine playing with less than 3, and 4 really is the sweet spot.

text_fidelity_a:
Nasco WA04313 Human Body Fat Replica, 5 lb. Most reviews mention the mind-boggling size of the model; I figured that it was because when we gain fatty tissue, it's distributed in a thin layer over our bodies, so seeing it as a lump would be surprising to most people.

     Even with the warnings, I was still shocked! It looked like it had to be 8-10 pounds, not a mere 5! And it FELT like 6-8 pounds...

After a while, I got curious as to why it seemed so disproportionately large. I'm aware that I consistently make terrible (truly awful) estimations of volumes, distances, and weights, so I measured it, just to get the actual numbers.

     My kitchen scale gave the model's mass as 5.293 pounds. That's a forgivable degree of error: 6%. Definitely closer than my awful guesstimate of 6-8 pounds.

     I used displacement to measure the volume as 11.75 cups. [I filled a container to overflowing with water. I added the model to displace some water, then removed the model. I carefully measured how much water I added to completely refill the container.]

     Google conversions gives 11.75 cups as being 169.6 in^3. Various sites list the volume of a pound of adipose tissue as being 29 in^3, 29.5 in^3, 30.08 in^3, and 30.42 in^3.

Using the model's volume and the lowest density, I calculate the model's representative mass as:
169.6 in^3 ÷ 30.42 in^3/lbs = 5.577 lbs

And using the highest density to calculate my model's "mass":
169.6 in^3 ÷ 29 in^3/lbs = 5.8 lbs (17% greater than 5 pounds, but well under my 8-10 pound guess.)

So whether you are measuring by weight or volume, the model is 6-17% oversized. That's far more accurate than seemed possible.

Obviously the manufacturer had to compromise between approximating the coloration, texture, pliablity, volume, and weight. I'm not a surgeon, so I'm clueless as to the accuracy of the coloration, texture, and pliablity. I am disappointed that the volume (which was the characteristic I was most interested in) was off by more than 5%.
text_fidelity_b: Nasco WA04313 Human Body Fat Replica, 5 lb.

text_fidelity_a: LEGO Minecraft Creeper BigFig and Ocelot Characters 21156 Buildable Toy Minecraft Figure Gift Set for Play and Decoration, New 2020 (184 Pieces) All three of my guys love Minecraft. For Halloween this past year, two of them even chose to dress up as Minecraft characters. We also love Lego around here, so the combination of the two is extra exciting. This is a fun set and the finished Creeper and Ocelot are cute. Their legs can actually move a bit when finished, which is entertaining. Our one complaint about this particular set, though, is the fact that the Creeper looks unfinished. I noticed it myself, but I didn't say anything about it. When my 6 year old got it, he commented about the unfinished look, too. So, it's definitely noticeable. The back of him doesn't get covered right(in our opinion), and it's left with the uncovered look of the bottom of a Lego piece. Two more pieces could have went such a long way with him. The same is true for the back of the head, backside, and tail of the Ocelot, but it's not as noticeable. (It's shown in the 360 degree drag and spin feature at the top of this page.) Otherwise, we're pleased with this set. It's a small set, so it doesn't take long to put together. Larger sets are sometimes more fun, but when time is on the lower side, this is a great kit, and the finished products are nice additions to other sets.

LEGO Creator 3in1 Twin Rotor Helicopter 31096 Building Kit (569 Pieces) One of these things is not like the others. The boat is pretty standard, as is the airplane. The Helicopter is all kinds of cool. The twin rotor blades spin, the hatch in back opens, and the winch is capable of lifting the buoy that comes with the kit.

It's an interesting way to put together a 3 in one kit. We built the helicopter first. It's the most difficult build in the box, uses the most pieces, has the most complexity, and is far and away the nicest looking model. Then we took that apart to build the rather uninspiring "super fast plane" and the "awesome hovercraft" that looks just like a chubby boat. You do not have the pieces in here to build all three at once and play with them together.

It's certainly nice to have a very cool model like this, and I love that there are kits nowadays that utilize the multiple instructions. I wish that the other models were a little more in line with the helicopter.

Luckily, we still had batteries (because we had to buy two packs) to replace the ones in the cars (the ones in the controllers were still good) and they played some more. They travel pretty good distance for a radio controlled car and they are relatively easy to maneuver for young kids. My 5 year old enjoyed playing with them for awhile (and the ferrets were terrified of them! They spent most of the day chasing the dog and ferrets around...which I suppose is entertaining. The little guy flies out of the car when the button on the side is depressed whether by the other car or if it hits against an object. He also yells like he's falling through the air! The bumper cars resemble an airboat to me. The construction is good IMO and its small enough for little hands to handle easily but large enough to see it coming.

The kids enjoyed playing with them for awhile but like most things it gets tossed to the side when something new comes along.

text_fidelity_a:
Venn Board Game | Family Game for 2+ Players | Cooperative & Competitive Gameplay Variations | Creative Word Association Game Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Ages 10+ Venn is a party game that plays a large number of players, and it comes with a competitive mode and a cooperative mode. The cooperative mode was not fun for our family, so we'll focus on the competitive game. In this game, you use cards with odd artwork to get your teammates to guess a set of three out of twelve possible games. The cards go in one of the seven different sections of a three-way Venn Diagram like you used to see in school. Using the clues you're given, you attempt to identify the three chosen words that the card placer is going for.

There are some fun times to be had here, but a few problems as well. The art is meant to be odd and unusual, but a good amount of it is just plain bad - characters are off-center, objects look like they're floating in the background, etc - and the cards are hard to use because they don't actually fit inside the sections of the Venn diagram. The words are usually very descriptive, but there are also some bad word chocies in the deck like "great" or "interesting" which could literally mean anything.

Unfortunately, this is competing in a crowded market - competitive, team-based family games have been done to death, so if you want to stand out, choose a game like Codenames or Just One or So Clover or...well, there's a lot of them, and they're mostly better than this.
text_fidelity_b: Venn Board Game | Family Game for 2+ Players | Cooperative & Competitive Gameplay Variations | Creative Word Association Game Featuring Unique Gameplay & Custom Artwork | Ages 10+

text_fidelity_a:
The Secret Life of Pets - Snowball Walking Talking Pets Figure This is a 'cute' little toy. I like the expression on his face. We've had fun playing with it for the past couple weeks.

Some things that you might want to know about it if you're considering buying one.

The instructions suggest replacing the two AAA batteries when you take the figure out of the package - the two that come in it are for 'in-store' demonstration purposes. Opening the battery compartment I found that the supplied batteries are pretty decent alkaline ones. Still, I replaced the ones in mine as I hate it when batteries go dead in a device and then leak. Something to maybe mention - the battery compartment is secured with a screw, so that small hands can't get into it.

The tail on the rabbit acts as the on/off switch. There are three setting - On, Off, and Demo. In the demonstration mode the figure talks and the wheels turn for a few seconds and then stops. When in the On position, the figure says a phrase - the wheels go for awhile and then it stops and repeats the cycle. The figure has three wheels - two fixed wheels seem to drive it's motion and a third rotates to make the figure go in different directions. Our rabbit seems to have a habit of finding the nearest corner and parking itself in it. The figure's eyes move a bit when it's in running around (although it's hard to see with the way it's eyes are set).

The figure comes with a separate carrot prop. Which the rabbit is suppose to hold in it's one hand - ours kept dropping his. So I took a piece of the white string that had secured the toy to the package and tied the carrot to his hand- you can't really even see it.

The rabbit talks, and I know it's suppose to be Kevin Hart doing a 'cartoon' voice - but it's really hard to understand what it's suppose to be saying. Hopefully when the movie comes out the phrases will be more recognizable.

All in all I like this figure and I'm looking forward to seeing the movie.
text_fidelity_b: The Secret Life of Pets - Snowball Walking Talking Pets Figure

I was saying how fun it was and how these squishy toys are great for stress relief (which they are), and how it kind of smelled like vanilla or egg nog.  I thought it was such a cute little doll. It just started coming apart.  You can see what I mean in the 4th and 5th photos.  This should not happen with any squishy toy, or any other toy for that matter.  I consider this a safety concern and am giving this toy one star for this reason.
